who: Mohammed Hassen Ali, historian of Africa at Georgia State University, doctorate in African history from London.

evidence.says: Kefentse's 2015 dissertation names Mohammed Hassen Ali as director and Mohammed Ali as committee chair; the acknowledgements call him Mohammed H. Ali.
Georgia State identifies Mohammed Hassen Ali as an emeritus associate professor of history, educated in African history at London and specializing in Ethiopian and Oromo history.
The candidate authority identifies the author of Ethnicity, Politics, and Society in Northeast Africa and The Oromo Language as a trained economist with a PhD in economic sciences.

notes: The dissertation establishes the supervisor's fuller name. The candidate is a different author with a different doctoral field.

who: Donald W. Engels, ancient historian at the University of Arkansas, PhD in history, Pennsylvania, 1976.

evidence.says: Donathan Taylor's institutional biography says his 1997 Arkansas dissertation, The Logistics of the Roman Army in North Africa, was supervised by Donald W. Engels.
LC's Roman Corinth citation identifies Donald Engels as an Arkansas history professor with a history PhD from Pennsylvania in 1976.

notes: Direct student-supervisor confirmation and the authority record agree on institution, field and doctoral university.

who: Pekka K. Hamalainen, historian of Europe at Wisconsin–Madison, PhD Indiana, 1966.

evidence.says: Wisconsin lists Pekka Hamalainen as adviser to Carol Adamson in 1986–1987 and Svein Myklebust in 1979–1980, with the supplied dissertation titles.
Wisconsin identifies its emeritus professor as Pekka K. Hamalainen, PhD Indiana 1966, interested in Western European studies and author of books on Finland and German reunification.
The candidate authority identifies the author of Lakota America, an Oxford professor of American history previously teaching Spanish Borderlands and Native American history at UC Santa Barbara.
The candidate's Oxford profile describes a historian of North America, previously at Texas A&M and UC Santa Barbara, author of The Comanche Empire and Lakota America.

notes: The Wisconsin European historian and the candidate American historian are different people.

who: James D. Anderson, University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign historian of education, specializing in African American education.

evidence.says: The university repository names James D. Anderson as director of research and committee co-chair for Perzavia Praylow's 2012 history PhD on coeducation and leadership at Fisk.
Illinois identifies James D. Anderson as an emeritus education professor whose scholarship concerns the history of African American education.
The candidate authority is James D. Anderson, also catalogued as James Douglas Anderson, author of Education for Servitude.

notes: The thesis repository resolves the abbreviated AHA name to the James D. Anderson candidate.

who: John Craig, historian of the English Reformation at Simon Fraser University since 1994, PhD Cambridge, 1992.

evidence.says: Craig's university biography gives a Cambridge doctorate in 1992 and arrival at Simon Fraser in September 1994; his research concerns early modern English religion.
The candidate authority is John M. Craig, author of Lucia Ames Mead and the American Peace Movement; a publisher confirmation places him at Slippery Rock College.

notes: The candidate is John M. Craig of Slippery Rock, not the Simon Fraser Reformation historian.

who: James W. Anderson, University of Georgia history professor, documented there in the 1970s and subsequently emeritus.

evidence.says: Georgia's History Department identifies its emeritus professor as James W. Anderson.
Georgia lists James Anderson of History among teaching award recipients in 1973, 1974 and 1976, establishing the relevant period.
Candidate p-1489 is James A. Anderson of UNC Greensboro, author of The Rebel Den of Nùng Trí Cao.
Candidate p-106114 is James Maxwell Anderson, a Calgary emeritus professor and author on Iberian studies and Romance linguistics.
Candidate James D. Anderson became an Illinois faculty member in 1974 and specializes in the history of African American education.
Candidate J. L. Anderson is Joseph L. Anderson, PhD Iowa State 2005; his CV records academic appointments beginning in 2001, including West Georgia in 2006–2008 and Mount Royal from 2008.

notes: Georgia identifies James W. Anderson; the four candidates resolve to different full names and academic careers.

who: Patrick Baker, historian of ancient Greece and Hellenistic institutions at Université Laval.

evidence.says: Laval's December 2017 defence announcement names Patrick Baker of Laval as director of Kale Coghlan's thesis, Écrire le monde, matching the supplied dissertation title.
Laval identifies Baker as an ancient Greek historian specializing in military institutions, Hellenistic cities and Greek epigraphy.
The candidate is the author of Italian Renaissance Humanism in the Mirror, a Humboldt University researcher with a Harvard history PhD from 2009, specializing in Renaissance humanism.

notes: The Laval ancient historian and the candidate Renaissance historian are different people.

who: Katherine Verdery, anthropologist of Romania, Michigan professor 1997–2005 and subsequently at CUNY; PhD Stanford, 1977.

evidence.says: Michigan's Anthropology and History program explicitly names Katherine Verdery as adviser to Oana Mateescu in 2017 and Emanuela Grama in 2010, with both supplied dissertation titles.
Verdery's institutional CV lists a Stanford anthropology PhD in 1977, a Michigan professorship in 1997–2005, and a CUNY appointment from 2005; her specialization includes Romania.
The candidate authority identifies Katherine Verdery as author of Transylvanian Villagers and work on national ideology in Eastern Europe.

notes: Both supervisory relationships are explicitly confirmed despite the dissertations' completion after her move to CUNY.
